question.text: Diamond has a three dimensional structure of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math> atoms formed by covalent bonds. The structure of diamond has face centred cubic lattice where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>50</mn><mo>%</mo></math> of the tetrahedral voids are also occupied by carbon atoms. The number of carbon atoms present per unit cell of diamond is ________.

solution.text:
Carbon atoms occupy FCC lattice points as well as half of the tetrahedral voids

therefore number of carbon atoms atoms per unit cell =8
